newsitem.title: USA: Delta Air stock falls as costs seen increasing.
newsitem.headline: Delta Air stock falls as costs seen increasing.

text.p: Delta Air Lines Inc. stock fell further Friday after the nation's third largest air carrier said it expected its costs to increase.
Shares in the Atlanta-based airline, which lost $5 Thursday despite solid third-quarter earnings, fell by $3 to $90.125 Friday after it warned about future costs.

Delta, which returned to profitability with net income of $189 million in the three months ended March 31, said Friday it expected its current-quarter unit costs, or costs per available seat mile, to increase 5.8 percent over the third quarter.
Delta also said it expected available seat miles for the fourth quarter ending June 30 to increase 2.9 percent over the third quarter.

The airline is facing increased pilot training costs related to its trans-Atlantic realignment, which was announced in January, as well as higher profit-sharing and incentive payments for employees, spokeswoman Kim King said.
Delta also expects additional costs due to a higher volume of passengers carried during the busy spring and summer season, King said.

The airline also will face additional advertising and marketing costs to announce upgrades in its trans-Atlantic business class service. Delta is expected to announce the new advertising campaign next week.

While Delta's move to improve its business class will increase near-term costs, the transition is necessary to improve customer service and ammenities to attract more high-paying business class customers, analysts said.
"It's a trade-off. High costs, if done correctly, means higher revenues. It could work out for a better impact on revenues," said Brian Harris, an airline analyst with Lehman Brothers.
"It is consistent with the whole programme of fleet upgrades. It's a wise move," said Timothy Ross, an airline analyst with SBC Warburg.
Delta declined to comment on how the additional costs may affect its fourth-quarter earnings.
Ross said the airline told analysts in a conference call late Thursday that it expects revenue unit growth to exceed cost growth.
Delta's stock started to slide Thursday as investors cashed in on the airline's strong third-quarter earnings after a recent rise in its stock price.
The stock continued to tumble Friday as investors became more concerned about near-term costs, analysts said.
